title: Telangana's Ramappa Temple used light bricks to ease its roof load
body: Work on the Ramappa Temple at Palampet began in 1213 CE. Builders made the stepped tower above the temple from lightweight porous bricks while using carved stone elsewhere in the building.
takeaway: A lighter material high in a building reduces the load that its columns and walls must carry.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Kakatiya Rudreshwara Temple (2021)
visual: the stepped brick tower of Ramappa Temple rising above dark stone pillars

title: Spain's Vizcaya Bridge carries traffic in a suspended gondola
body: The 1893 Vizcaya Bridge near Bilbao has a 160-metre span. Instead of crossing on the upper structure, people and vehicles ride a platform that hangs from it and travels just above the water.
takeaway: Tall ships can pass underneath the upper span while road users cross close to the riverbank level.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Vizcaya Bridge (2006)
visual: a passenger platform hanging from cables below the tall Vizcaya Bridge

title: A Chilean mining town used a staircase as its main route
body: Built in 1905 on an Andean slope about 2,000 metres above sea level, Sewell occupied ground too steep for wheeled traffic. A long staircase ran up from the railway station, with public squares along it.
takeaway: A staircase can organise a neighbourhood just as a main road does on flatter ground.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sewell Mining Town (2006)
visual: a long staircase climbing between bright wooden houses in the Andes

title: A 67 km Alpine railway needed 42 tunnels and galleries
body: The Albula railway opened in 1904 through the Swiss Alps. Along its 67 km route, the line crosses 144 viaducts and bridges and runs through 42 tunnels and covered galleries.
takeaway: In steep terrain, a railway's length tells you little about how much structure is needed to make it usable.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Rhaetian Railway (2008)
visual: a mountain railway on a curved stone viaduct above a wooded gorge
